AGENDA
  GLENDALE ARTS AND CULTURE COMMISSION
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the City webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, Amazon Fire, iOS and
Android devices using a free app called Cablecast and choosing "Glendale TV" from the menu.
Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas.
Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. For public comments and questions during the
meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that
agenda item is discussed. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for
assistance, please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. The City Clerk’ office should be notified 72 hours (three
business days) or as soon as practicable for requests regarding sign language translation and
Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are
received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review
in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting or as soon as
practicable. Please specify the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City
provided interpreters is not required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak
in their native language.

CITY OF GLENDALE
  ARTS and CULTURE COMMISSION
  Minutes of Regular Meeting

  Thursday, March 21, 2024, at 10:00 a.m.
1.  ROLL CALL
  •  The meeting was called to order on March 21, 2024, at 10:03 a.m.
  •  Present: Vice Chair Yank, Commissioners Tufenkian, Viar, Zadorian, Aleksandryan, Pogosian,
  Chairperson Vidor
  •  Absent: None
  •  The Agenda for the March 21, 2024, Regular Meeting was posted on March 15, 2024, on the Bulletin
  Board outside City Hall.

2. CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the
  Commission or the audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such
  request before motion is proposed.
  a. Minutes of the February 15, 2024 Regular Arts and Culture Commission Meeting
  b. Minutes of the February 27, 2024 Special Arts and Culture Commission Meeting
  c. Minutes of the March 13, 2024 Special Arts and Culture Commission Meeting

  Moved:  Commissioner Viar
  Seconded :  Commissioner Zadorian

  Ayes:  Vice Chair Yank, Commissioners Tufenkian, Viar, Zadorian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  Commissioners Aleksandryan, Pogosian

3. INTRODUCTIONS AND PRESENTATIONS
  a. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Loreto Lopez, Program Coordinator
  • Ms. Lopez gave an overview of current and upcoming events at Glendale Library, Arts &
  Culture locations.

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to Items NOT a Part of this Agenda. Each Speaker is Allowed 5 Minutes.
  Members of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission may Question or Respond to the
  Speaker, but there will be no Debate or Decision. The Matter may be Referred to Staff
  Through the Commission Chair for Investigation and Report. – No Speakers

5. DISCUSSION ITEMS
a. Artsakh Avenue Re-Development Project: Update
  • Staff provided an update on the Artsakh Ave. Re-Development Project.
  • Sarkis Oganesyan, Deputy Director of Public Works/City Engineer provided an update on the Artsakh
  Ave. Re-Development Project.
  • Commission asked questions and provided their input.

  1
 b. Urban Art Fund: 2023 Fee Summary
  • Ms. Jennifer Fukutomi-Jones, Principal Arts & Culture Administrator, provided an overview of the 2023
  Urban Art Program Fee Summary and Overall Urban Art Program total. Commission asked questions
  and provided their input.

c. 2023-2024 Work Plan Progress Updates

  CITY WIDE ARTS
  Mural Ordinance – Update:
  •  Staff is working with the City Attorney’s Office on the final draft of the Mural Ordinance. The final draft will
  be scheduled for initial review by the Commission at an upcoming Regular Meeting of the Arts and
  Culture Commission.
  •  Commission asked questions and provided their input.

  NEIGHBORHOOD ARTS
  Adams Square Mini Park Gas Station Exhibits – Update:
  •  The Artist Review & Selection Committee for the Adams Square Mini Park Gas Station Exhibits met on
  March 13, 2024 to review proposals. Staff received 54 applications for consideration. Staff shared the
  proposed programming. Commission asked questions and provided their input.
  2024 Performance Series – Update:
  •  The Artist Review & Selection Committee for the 2024 Performance Series met on February 27, 2024
  to review proposals. Staff received 121 applications for consideration. Staff shared the proposed
  programming. Commission asked questions and provided their input.

  •  ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS – No update.

  •  MARKETING AND COMMUNICATIONS – No update.

6. COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
  • Vice Chair Yank suggested further discussion on Artsakh Re-Development Project delays and stated
  that she would like to brainstorm among the Commission on ideas that will move the project forward.
  Commissioner Tufenkian agreed and stated it was a great suggestion.
  • Commissioner Viar thanked Vice Chair Yank for her comment on the Artsakh project postponements
  and thanked the Committees for the music series performance selections and for the Adams Square
  Mini Park Gas Station art selections. Commissioner Viar invited everyone to attend the Transportation
  Center where fellow Chairperson Vidor is part of an ensemble that will be performing.
  • Commissioner Zadorian stated she wanted to confirm agendized discussions on Artsakh Re-
  Developments Project art postponements for next meeting.
  • Chair Vidor stated that its important to keep in touch with Public Works for major milestones and
  decision points and it would be helpful for the Commission decision making process to cooperate
  closely with them. Thanked the special committees for performance series and Adams Square Mini
  Gas Station art installations. Chair Vidor also welcome Sylvia of City Attorney’s office.
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones thanked Commissioner Tufenkian for being part of the City-Wide Public Art RFQ
  Committee and stated they had fantastic artists who applied for the RFQ, recommendations were made
  and LaBasse is working with finalists and the Montrose Circular benches will be prioritized.
  • Chair Vidor asked for an update on the Central Park artwork project. Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated that
  plans for Central Park are still being finalized but Staff is working closely with Parks.
  • Commission thanked Staff for their work on all the Commission programs and projects.

  2
 7. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS- None

8. ADJOURNMENT 10:49 a.m.
The next Regular Meeting of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission is Thursday, April
18, 2024, at 10:00 AM at City Council Chambers – 613 E. Broadway (2 Floor) Glendale, CA
91206.
